If you had a grip on the reality of Gaza, if you cared at all about the people of Gaza, you would be cheering this progress report and working to free the Gazans from Hamas.

It's really amazing how you twisted his words. You're literally criticizing him for feeding the Gazans.

Here's what he actually said in this video: "Because it's become this whole industrial complex of aid and a lot of it was stolen to fund a terrorist organization, so we changed the way the aid was done. We flooded aid into Gaza, and now it has one of the lowest malnutrition rates in the world".

Rebuilding wouldn't take so long if Hamas weren't stealing the food and obstructing progress.

tweets.body:
The argument isn't about hunger. It's about truth.

If the definition of famine is universally applied everywhere except for one place, it means somebody's lying to you, that they're manipulating you.

You see the end result, the destruction, and you succumb to the endless lies, and then you draw the wrong conclusions about how they lost their homes, why they don't have critical infrastructure, and what actually happened to their hospitals.

Before the war, Gaza had more hospitals per capita than Israel but used them as military bases and torture chambers.

Before the war, Gaza received more aid per capita than anybody else in the world and then proceded to use that aid to build the largest bunker system in the world instead of infrastructure and an economy, a bunker system, by the way, that no Gazan civilian was allowed to use during the war.

Before the war and throughout the war, Israel provided free aid (and continues to do so) to Gaza even as Hamas and its allies were lobbing thousands upon thousands of rockets at Israels civilians, aid that Hamas stole at gunpoint and sold at unbelievable prices to its own people. The argument that the aid could be "cut off at any time" is a straw man.

If you've accepted that the famine was a lie, and if truth matters to you, it behooves you to at least consider that some of the other "facts" you think you know about the conflict might also be lies.

He wasn't. Your knee-jerk racist reaction is exactly what he's talking about.

But to put things in perspective, I will.

Hamas is a genocidal fascist terrorist organization that has been brutally and savaegly murdering Israelis, intentionally sabotaging all peace efforts for decaddes, and inciting antisemitic hatred worldwide. It is responsible for the October 7th pogrom.

But it is not unreasonable or far-fetched to talk about, or rather decry, Ben Gvir and Smotrich's racism and terrorist ties. Ben Gvir has literally been convicted on terrorism-related charges. And now they're in the government coalition turning the police against the citizens they're supposed to protect, inciting violence against protesters, encouraging illegal settlements, intentionally inflaming already troubled global opinion against Israel, and working dilligently to dismantle Israeli democracy from within.

So Hamas is obviously ten thousand times worse than Ben Gvir and Smotrich ever were or could be, but even if we completely defeat Hamas and its ilk in every war forever, this struggle will never end if we can't look at our own failings and fix them the same way that Alkhatib is trying to do for his people.

The first simple fact is that there are probably around 16 million people in Israel and Palestine, about half of whom are Jewish and half Arab.

It is brave people like you, working tirelessly to bring about that shared future, who give us hope.

tweets.body:
I agree completely but would add another important aspect: demonizing Israel and the Jews as we fight for our survival makes it very hard for us patriotic Israelis to raise legitimate criticism.

The constant spreading of explicitly blatant lies forces us to prioritize our existential fight against the libels and defamations over the criminality and disputed war policies.

And instead of supporting the majority of Israelis who believe that we should wage this war more justly even though it was brutally thrust upon us, the nonstop slander and manipulation push us to respond with unambiguous clarity, uncluttered, as it were, by nuance.

So instead of pressuring the army and government to more strictly enforce ethical boundaries and to further lessen the impact of the war on innocent civilians, we are compelled to stand instead against the immense onslaught of vile hatred and its dangerous repercussions.
